# Market-Entry Campaign: Health Supplement, Japan
## In a post-scandal category, restraint is not a compliance cost — it is the entire persuasion strategy

**Illustrative case used throughout:** a mid-size Western wellness brand launching a sleep-quality supplement (GABA + a lactic-acid bacterium strain) into Japan, targeting 40–59-year-old urban office workers. Figures are illustrative; regulatory text must be confirmed with Japanese counsel before any asset is produced, as this regime has changed twice in the last three years.

**Why Japan is the right teaching case:** it is one of the few markets with a *notification-based functional claims regime* that lets a food make a specific physiological claim — and it just went through a trust shock (the 2024 red-yeast-rice/beni-kōji harm incident) that made the whole category suspect. So the market simultaneously permits more than most and forgives less than any. Every choice has to be defended.

---

## 0. Three decisions before any creative brief is written

1. **Your regulatory lane is a product decision, not a copy decision.** Japan offers three doors: **FOSHU** (特定保健用食品, individually approved, slow, expensive, highest trust), **Foods with Nutrient Function Claims** (栄養機能食品, self-certified against a fixed vitamin/mineral list, no room for a differentiated story), and **Foods with Function Claims** (機能性表示食品/FFC, notification to the Consumer Affairs Agency backed by a human RCT on the finished product or a systematic review on the functional ingredient at the used dose). Which door you walk through determines the sentence you are allowed to say for the next five years. Choose it before you appoint an agency — not after, when the deck already contains a headline you cannot legally run.
2. **Ethics and effectiveness are the same programme here, and this is not a platitude.** After beni-kōji, Japanese consumers, drugstore buyers and the CAA all discount the category. The scarce asset is not attention; it is credibility. That means substantiation, disclosure and adverse-event handling *are the campaign content*, not the legal overhead behind it. A brand that publishes its trial, its GMP certificate and its complaint line is not being cautious — it is taking the only available differentiated position.
3. **You are the cause of your own compliance failures.** Almost no company decides to make an illegal claim. It happens because the marketing scorecard is first-order ROAS and CAC, and someone downstream — usually an affiliate or an unbriefed influencer — closes the gap with the words "cures," "immunity up," or an undisclosed paid post. **Change the KPI first** (§6). A compliance manual laid over a CAC-only scorecard is theatre with a budget line.

---

## 1. Unbundle: "cultural adaptation" is five different problems with five different instruments

| | **Hard law (claims)** | **Soft law & platform norms** | **Belief system** | **Trust & channel structure** | **Rhetorical convention** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Content** | Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Act (薬機法) ban on medicinal efficacy claims for foods; Health Promotion Act; FFC notification scope; Premiums & Misleading Representations Act (景表法) | JFTC's 2023 designation of undisclosed paid promotion ("stealth marketing") as an unfair representation; No.1-claim substantiation norms; industry ad-review bodies; Rakuten/Amazon/Yahoo listing rules | Health as **整える** (attuning, regulating) rather than boosting; 未病 (pre-disease); 体質 (constitutional type); 腸活 (gut care); 睡眠負債 (sleep debt); seasonal body logic | Drugstore/pharmacy staff as the credibility node; physician authority high; @cosme / Rakuten / Amazon JP review volume; LINE (~95m users) as the CRM layer; mail-order dominant for 65+ | Restraint reads as confidence; superlatives read as fraud; indirect benefit framing; before/after imagery is culturally *and* legally toxic; specificity of dose and study beats emotional promise |
| **Failure signature** | Measures order, surcharge, forced retraction | Silent de-listing; influencer backlash; 5ch/X pile-on | Message lands as foreign and aggressive; no purchase intent | No shelf, no repeat purchase | Perceived as an American infomercial |
| **Wrong instrument** | "Legal will check the copy at the end" | Bulk micro-influencer buy | Translating your home-market brief | Performance media only, DTC only | Louder, bigger, more testimonials |
| **Right instrument** | Claim–evidence gap audit *before* creative (§2) | Written disclosure obligations + affiliate kill switch (§4, Tier 1) | Qualitative belief mapping; reframe to 整える | Pharmacist/staff education as campaign phase one | Under-claim, over-document |

**The critical connection:** all five collapse onto one asset — **a single, notified, verbatim claim sentence with a documented evidence pack behind it.** Without it you have no legal copy, no drugstore listing conversation, no defensible influencer brief, and no answer to the post-scandal question every consumer now asks. It is the cheapest thing on the list and it must exist first.

---

## 2. The diagnostic that requires no focus group: the claim–evidence gap

Stop debating which benefit "resonates." Run every candidate message through two questions with knowable answers:

- **CS — Claim Sought:** the sentence marketing wants to say.
- **ES — Evidence Standing:** the strongest claim the existing dossier can defend under the target lane, on the *finished product at the marketed dose*.

**Exposure is the gap.** Where ES ≥ CS, run it. Where CS exceeds ES, you have three options and only three: reduce the claim, buy the evidence, or drop the message. "Soften the wording" is not a fourth option — implied medicinal efficacy is judged on total impression, including imagery and testimonials, not on the literal words.

| Candidate message | Evidence standing | Verdict | Cost to close the gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Helps maintain sleep quality — supports feeling rested on waking" | Human RCT on finished product, n=120, primary endpoint met | **Run it, verbatim, everywhere** | €0 — already paid |
| "Relieves temporary stress from daily life" | SR on the functional ingredient at our dose | Run only if a second notification is filed and accepted | ~€60k, 4–6 months |
| "Supports immunity" | Mechanistic/in-vitro only | **Drop.** Reads as disease prevention; unsubstantiated | Not buyable at this budget |
| "Improves gut flora balance" | Strain-level data from a different dose | **Drop for launch.** Bridge study needed | ~€180k, 12 months |
| "No.1 recommended by pharmacists" | No independent survey | **Drop.** Requires a documented, independently run survey with disclosed methodology and basis | ~€40k + reputational fragility |
| "Cured my insomnia" (user testimonial) | N/A | **Prohibited.** Disease-treatment implication; also unusable even as UGC | Never |

**Design rule:** the notified claim sentence appears *word-for-word* in every asset, including influencer captions and affiliate landing pages, and is the **only** efficacy statement any party may make. Everything else in the campaign is context, ritual, and proof — never a second promise. One sentence, one thousand placements.

---

## 3. Price the status quo — the ethical tail is a cash event, not a reputational abstraction

| | |
|---|---|
| Planned Japan year-1 net revenue | €12m |
| Surcharge exposure under the Premiums & Misleading Representations Act (≈3% of relevant sales over the violation period, with an uplift for repeat offenders — confirm current text) | **€0.4m+ per violating SKU-period** |
| Forced retraction, corrective notice, asset re-shoot, agency re-brief | **€0.6–0.9m** |
| E-commerce de-listing (Rakuten/Amazon JP) for 8 weeks | **€1.4m revenue, plus review-ranking loss that does not recover** |
| Drugstore chain de-shelving after a public order — recovery cycle | **12–24 months; frequently permanent for a new foreign brand** |
| Subscription (定期購入) complaint cluster → Consumer Affairs escalation | **Category-wide enforcement attention; the single most-policed dark pattern in the market** |
| Cost of doing it properly: finished-product RCT + FFC notification + counsel + pre-publication ad review + third-party grievance line | **~€450k once, then ~€90k/yr** |

Two conclusions for one slide. First, **the compliant path is cheaper than one enforcement event**, and enforcement probability for an aggressive supplement launch in Japan is not low. Second, the category's post-scandal trust discount means the compliant path also *sells better* — which is the rare case where the ethical argument does not need the ethical argument.

---

## 4. The intervention ladder — climb it in order

| Tier | Content | Cost | Time | Reversibility |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **0 — See it** | Regulatory lane decision; claim–evidence gap audit; competitor claim sweep (what has actually been notified, and what has been withdrawn); belief mapping with 40–59 urban consumers on sleep, fatigue and 整える language; pharmacist and drugstore-buyer interviews | Low | 6–10 wks | Total |
| **0b — Build the asset** | FFC notification filed and accepted; GMP/third-party certification for the dosage form; adverse-event intake process and reporting SLA stood up **before** first sale; plain-Japanese evidence page including null findings | ~€450k | 4–7 months | Total |
| **1 — Contract for it** | Written claim-scope annex binding agency, PR firm, affiliates and every KOL; mandatory disclosure wording (PR表記) in the first visible line; affiliate whitelist with pre-approved creative only; **kill switch** and clawback for off-claim copy; monthly third-party ad-monitoring sweep; subscription terms compliant with final-confirmation-screen rules and one-click cancellation | Low | 4–8 wks | High |
| **2 — Run it** | Pharmacist education → owned/CRM → earned/native → paid retargeting, in that order (§5) | Moderate opex | 3–9 months | High |
| **3 — Restructure** | FOSHU application for the flagship claim; second notification for the stress claim; clinical collaboration with a Japanese university; physician-channel line extension | High | 18–36 months | Low |

**Design rules.** Tier 0 and 0b are unconditional. **Never buy media before the notification is accepted** — the resulting copy will be either illegal or unpersuasive. An influencer without a written claim-scope annex is not a channel; they are an uninsured liability. And never launch a subscription offer whose cancellation path is harder than its sign-up path: in this market that is not aggressive marketing, it is the fastest known route to a regulator's inbox.

---

## 5. The campaign

**Positioning:** *整える* — attuning, not boosting. Japanese health discourse rewards restoration of rhythm and balance and is actively suspicious of enhancement language ("免疫力アップ" is both a cultural and a legal red flag). The product is framed as helping return sleep to
